title: Minimax RMST Regret for Policy Learning under Limited Treatment and Censoring Overlap
banked_reason: D0.5.G: supplied-design two-sided frontier and conditional unknown-design algebra only; paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4 field floor, salvageable=false, while math and decision panels pass.
gap_reasons: The note proves a two-sided finite-sample minimax regret profile only for supplied treatment probabilities and a supplied common censoring curve, not for unknown or heterogeneous censoring designs.

The unknown-design proposition is conditional algebra: it assumes the policy-support relative band and supplies no primitive nuisance model, construction, or rate, so it does not extend the operational frontier.

The interval upper bound is honest, but its width converse concerns an externally supplied rare-arm policy on a point-mass subclass and does not establish sharpness for arbitrary learned policies or procedures reusing training observations.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a two-sided full-curve RMST regret profile for supplied treatment probabilities and a supplied common censoring curve, plus honest independent-holdout value intervals. Source and Lean statement mismatches were repaired, and the D0.5 math and decision panels passed. The field-tier framing fell short because heterogeneous unknown-design adaptation remains an open question and the width lower bound applies only to a supplied rare-arm policy on a restricted subclass; the general referee assessed subfield tier.
tldr: The known-design problem is closed by a matching finite-sample minimax RMST-regret profile and an honest independent-holdout interval. The unknown heterogeneous-design extension remains open. Conditional on a supplied measurable one-sided band over the policy-relevant support, a separate algebraic proposition bounds profile inflation by \((1-\rho)^{-1/2}\), score bias by \(\rho\tau/(1-\rho)\), and all band and fallback penalties. It does not construct the band or assign nuisance rates.
gap: Among the theorem texts audited here, no result gives a matching arbitrary-lawful-common-G minimax upper and lower profile for binary causal VC-policy RMST regret, including jumps and zero interior follow-up.
fill: Establish or refute the proposed profile, its consistency and polynomial-tail consequences, and finite-sample conditional holdout inference with a supplied-policy-only lower-width benchmark; then characterize relative-error conditions for unknown-design adaptation.
